docs.title: API basics
docs.text: A short guide to how APIs work, using the calls from the FreshFlow project.

docs.title: What is an API
docs.text:
API is a messenger that allows two different software applications to communicate and exchange information with each other.

For example, when you order food in a delivery app, the app sends your order to the restaurant's system through an API.

docs.title: Parts of a request
docs.text:
When an application communicates with another application using an API, it sends a request.

  • Method: what you want to do (GET, POST, PUT or DELETE).
  • URL: the address where you send the request.
  • Headers: extra information, such as the data type or an API key.
  • Body: the data you send, used with POST and PUT.

docs.title: Parts of a response
docs.text:
When an application sends a request to a server through an API, the server processes that request and sends back a response.

  • Status code: a number that tells you if it worked, such as 200, 201 or 404.
  • Body: the data that comes back, usually in JSON.

docs.title: JSON in one minute
docs.text:
JSON is a simple format used to store and exchange data between different applications.

It has five types: string (text), number, boolean (true or false), object (key and value pairs in curly brackets) and array (a list in square brackets).

{
  "title": "FreshFlow stock alert",
  "userId": 1,
  "sent": true,
  "tags": ["stock", "alert"]
}

docs.title: The 5 calls in the Postman collection
docs.text: # Call Method What it shows 1 Get all posts GET A list of items (200 OK) 2 Get one post GET One item by its ID (200 OK) 3 Create a post POST Sending JSON, getting 201 Created 4 Delete a post DELETE Removing an item 5 FreshFlow - Create content POST Starting the FreshFlow n8n workflow through a webhook

docs.title: Try the collection yourself
docs.text:
1. Download postman/freshflow-api-basics.postman_collection.json from this repository.
  2. In Postman, click Import and choose the file.
  3. Calls 1 to 4 work straight away, because they use a free test API.
  4. For call 5, create an environment with a variable named freshflow_webhook_url and paste your own n8n webhook URL. The URL in the file is only a placeholder.

This page explains one API call, the building block behind the FreshFlow writer, checker and translator steps.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import anthropic
from google.colab import userdata

# Read the API key from a secret. Never type the key into the code.
client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=userdata.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"))

response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-haiku-5-5",
    max_tokens=500,
    system="You are the FreshFlow content writer. Follow the brand guide and the 10 compliance rules.",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Write a 2-line product intro for our inventory tracking software."}
    ],
)

print(response.content[0].text)

If you run this outside Google Colab, replace the userdata line with an environment variable:

import os
client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"])

docs.title: What each part does
docs.text: Part Meaning anthropic.Anthropic(...) Creates a connection to the API using your key model Which Claude model answers. FreshFlow uses claude-haiku-5-5 max_tokens The longest reply allowed. A token is about three-quarters of a word system Standing instructions: role, brand guide and rules messages The conversation. Here it holds one user request response.content[0].text The text of Claude's reply

docs.title: How FreshFlow uses it
docs.text: Step system holds messages holds Writer Brand guide, rules, and the output format (JSON) The content request Checker The 10 rules and the pass, fail or unsure format The writer's draft Translator The glossary of terms that must stay exact The approved draft

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error Likely cause Fix Authentication error Wrong or missing key Check the secret name and value Credit error No API credit on the account Add credit in the Anthropic Console Model not found Wrong model name Check the spelling of model Reply cut off max_tokens too low Increase max_tokens

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Warning

Never put your API key in code or commit it to GitHub. Keep it in a secret or an environment variable. If the key is ever shown publicly, delete it in the Console and create a new one.

docs.title: API quick start
docs.text: This page shows how to start the FreshFlow workflow with one cURL command, and what each answer means. For every field and response, see the API reference.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  • The FreshFlow workflow running in n8n, with its Webhook node set to the POST method.
  • Your own webhook address from the Webhook node.
  • A terminal that has curl (Git Bash, macOS Terminal and most Linux terminals have it).

Note

The addresses on this page are placeholders. Replace YOUR-N8N-HOST and your-webhook-path with your own values. Never share your real webhook address in a public place.

docs.title: Step 1: Save your address
docs.text:
Save your webhook address in a variable, so you do not type it again and again:

export FRESHFLOW_URL="https://YOUR-N8N-HOST/webhook-test/your-webhook-path"

The address has two forms:

Mode Address starts with When it works Test https://YOUR-N8N-HOST/webhook-test/ For one call, after you click Execute workflow in n8n Production https://YOUR-N8N-HOST/webhook/ Any time the workflow is active

docs.title: Step 2: Send a request
docs.text:
The body has one field, request. Write what you want and the facts the post may use.

curl -X POST "$FRESHFLOW_URL" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"request": "Write a short LinkedIn post about our new inventory tracking feature. Use only these facts: live stock counts for each shop, an alert when stock drops below 10 units, and mobile support. Do not add benefits or results that are not listed. Do not mention price."}'

docs.title: Step 3: Read the answer
docs.text:
A good call returns this:

{"message": "Workflow was started"}

Warning

This answer means the workflow started. It does not mean the post is ready. The finished post is saved to Notion, not returned in the answer.

Open your FreshFlow review table in Notion to see the post, its status and the checker notes. A new row can take about a minute to appear.

docs.title: What the answers mean
docs.text: What you see What it means What to do 200 and {"message": "Workflow was started"} The workflow started. The post is not finished yet. Open the review table in Notion and find the post. 404 and "The requested webhook ... is not registered" You used the test address, and n8n is not listening. Click Execute workflow in n8n, then send the call again. The test address works for one call each time. 200, but no post appears in Notion The request field is missing or empty. The answer is still 200, because the workflow starts first and fails inside. Check that the body has a request field with text. Then look at the failed run in the n8n Executions list. 200, and the post is saved with the status Needs human review The checker found a sentence that is not backed by your facts. The reason is in the Checker Notes column. Read the note, fix the post or the request, and send the call again if needed. 200, and the post is saved with the status Refused The request has no facts, so the content check refused to write the post. Add the facts the post may use, then send the call again.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Short answers to common questions about FreshFlow.

docs.title: Do I need to know Python?
docs.text: No. The Quick start takes you from nothing to a working FreshFlow test in about 30 minutes, and you do not need to know Python.

docs.title: What accounts do I need?
docs.text:
You need:

  • An Anthropic account with API credit, and an API key
  • A Google account (for Google Colab)
  • An n8n Cloud account (the free trial lasts 14 days)
  • A Notion account

docs.title: Where should I keep my API key?
docs.text: Store it as a secret. In Google Colab, open the key icon in the left sidebar, add a secret named ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and paste the key as its value. Never paste the key into a file you upload to GitHub. See Step 1 of the Quick start.

docs.title: What do the writer, checker and translator do?
docs.text: The writer drafts the content using the brand guide. The checker tests a draft against the 10 compliance rules. The translator translates approved content into Telugu using a glossary. See the Glossary for other terms.

docs.title: Can I trust the checker?
docs.text: Not on its own. The checker is an AI model, so it can miss problems or flag good content. Human review is the safety net. The 10 rules and the company are made up for this demo. Read more on How it works.

docs.title: My API call shows an error. What should I do?
docs.text: Check the table of common errors on the API call page. It lists the likely cause and the fix for a wrong or missing key, no API credit, a wrong model name and a reply that is cut off.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Short meanings of the terms used in the FreshFlow docs.

Term Meaning API A way for one program to ask another program to do something. FreshFlow uses the Claude API to write, check and translate content API key A secret code that proves you are allowed to use an API. Never share it or commit it to GitHub Writer The AI step that drafts the content using the brand guide Checker The AI step that tests a draft against the 10 compliance rules Translator The AI step that translates approved content into Telugu using a glossary System prompt Standing instructions sent with every request: the role, the brand guide and the rules Token A small piece of text. One token is about three-quarters of a word JSON A simple text format for data, used to pass results between workflow steps n8n A tool that connects steps into one automated workflow Workflow A chain of steps that runs in order, from the form to the Notion table Compliance rule A written rule that content must follow before a person can publish it Needs Human Review A status that means the checker is not sure, so a person decides Prompt library A Google Sheet that keeps every version of a prompt, with notes on what changed

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: FreshFlow uses two AI roles. A writer drafts content. A checker reviews the draft against the rules. Separating the two roles means the checker is not grading its own work.

docs.title: Workflow steps
docs.text: Step Node in n8n What it does 1 Content request form Receives the content request 2 Writer Drafts the content using the brand guide and returns JSON 3 Parse writer output Reads the writer's JSON so later steps can use it 4 Checker Tests the draft against the 10 brand and compliance rules 5 Parse checker result Reads the checker's result 6 Set final status Sets final_status 7 Translator Translates approved content into Telugu using a glossary 8 Parse translation Reads the Telugu translation 9 Save to Notion Saves the row in the "FreshFlow Content Review" table Error path Save error to Notion If the Writer step fails, saves the error in Notion

docs.title: The three outcomes
docs.text:
Status Meaning What happens next Approved The draft passes every rule, or the checker fixed it and explained the changes Content is translated and saved for human review before publishing Refused The request cannot be written safely, or has no facts to work from Saved as refused, not translated Needs Human Review The checker is unsure, or the request is too vague A person reads it and decides

Examples from test runs:

  • A request that only said the product "saves time", with no proof or detail, went to Needs Human Review in an earlier test.
  • A request for a stock tracking intro with no product facts was refused, and the checker asked for facts.
  • A request asking for a guaranteed 40% cost cut and a competitor comparison was approved after the checker removed those claims and explained the changes in Checker Notes.

docs.title: Prompts and versions
docs.text:
• The system prompt holds the brand guide and the 10 compliance rules.
  • Every prompt change is saved as a new version in the prompt library, with a note on what changed and why.
  • Old versions are kept so you can compare results and go back if a change makes things worse.

docs.title: Testing method
docs.text:
1. Write 20 test requests: 8 normal and 12 tricky.
  2. Run all 20 with the current prompt and score each result.
  3. Fix the prompt based on the failures and save it as a new version.
  4. Run the same 20 again and compare.
  5. Run new requests through the full n8n workflow to check the three outcomes.

The same test set is reused each time so results can be compared fairly.

docs.title: Telugu translation
docs.text:
• A glossary lists terms that must not change, such as prices and disclaimers.
  • A pricing test confirmed that the disclaimer and the amount (Rs 4,999) stayed exact in the Telugu output.
  • A Telugu reader (the author) checked the output.
  • Refused requests are not translated.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
Note

The checker is an AI model, so it can miss problems or flag good content. Human review is the safety net.

  • The 10 rules and the company are made up for this demo.
  • Tests were run on a small set of requests and do not prove accuracy at scale.

docs.title: Ideas for next steps
docs.text:
• Add an error log in Notion.
  • Add a short demo video.
  • Test with more tricky requests and track the results over time.

docs.title: HTTP status codes
docs.text: A status code is a 3-digit number that a server sends back after every API request. It tells you if the request worked.

docs.title: 200 OK
docs.text:
Your request worked, and the server sent back what you asked for.

What to do: nothing to fix. Read the data in the response.

docs.title: 201 Created
docs.text:
You asked the system to create something, and the system successfully created it.

What to do: nothing to fix. Save the new item's ID from the response.

docs.title: 400 Bad Request
docs.text:
You asked the server to do something, but your request contains incorrect or invalid information.

What to do: check your body for a missing field or bad JSON, fix it, and send again.

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
You are trying to access something, but you haven't proved your identity to the server.

What to do: check your API key or login details, and send again.

docs.title: 404 Not Found
docs.text:
You asked the server to show you something, but the server couldn't find it.

What to do: check the URL and the ID for spelling mistakes.

docs.title: 500 Server Error
docs.text:
Your request reached the server, but the server encountered a problem and couldn't complete your request.

What to do: this is not your mistake. Wait a little and try again. If it keeps happening, tell the server's owner.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This guide takes you from nothing to a working FreshFlow test in about 30 minutes. You do not need to know Python.

docs.text:
• Before you start
  • Step 1: Keep your API key safe
  • Step 2: Make your first API call
  • Step 3: Add the brand guide and rules
  • Step 4: Keep a prompt library
  • Step 5: Run the test set
  • Step 6: Build the workflow in n8n
  • Step 7: Add Telugu translation
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  • An Anthropic account with API credit, and an API key
  • A Google account (for Google Colab)
  • An n8n Cloud account (the free trial lasts 14 days)
  • A Notion account

docs.title: Step 1: Keep your API key safe
docs.text:
1. Copy your API key from the Anthropic Console.
  2. Store it as a secret. In Google Colab, open the key icon in the left sidebar, add a secret named ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and paste the key as its value.
  3. Never paste the key into a file you upload to GitHub.

docs.title: Step 2: Make your first API call
docs.text:
1. Open a new Google Colab notebook.
  2. Install the library by running this in a cell:
!pip install anthropic
  1. Copy the code from Claude API call into the next cell and run it.
  2. You should see a short reply from Claude. If you do, your key and credit work.

docs.title: Step 3: Add the brand guide and rules
docs.text:
1. Save the FreshFlow brand guide and the 10 compliance rules in one document.
  2. Paste them into the system prompt of the API call.
  3. Run a request that breaks a rule on purpose, for example one that promises a result the company cannot guarantee. The reply should refuse or flag it.

docs.title: Step 4: Keep a prompt library
docs.text:
1. Create a Google Sheet named "FreshFlow Prompt Library".
  2. Add one row per prompt version with these columns: version, date, prompt text, what changed, test result.
  3. Whenever you change the prompt, add a new row. Do not overwrite the old one.

docs.title: Step 5: Run the test set
docs.text:
1. Write 20 test requests: 8 normal and 12 tricky ones (for example, requests that ask for false claims or leave out required details).
  2. Run all 20 and score each result as pass or fail.
  3. Fix the prompt, save it as a new version, and run the same 20 again.
  4. Compare the two runs.

docs.title: Step 6: Build the workflow in n8n
docs.text:
1. Create a workflow named "FreshFlow content pipeline".
  2. Add the nodes in this order:
  3. Content request form (form trigger)
  4. Writer (Anthropic "Message a model")
  5. Parse writer output (Code)
  6. Checker (Anthropic "Message a model")
  7. Parse checker result (Code)
  8. Set final status (Edit Fields)
  9. Save to Notion
  10. Add your Anthropic and Notion credentials inside n8n. Do not put them in the workflow itself.
  11. Run a test from the form and check the row in Notion.

docs.title: Step 7: Add Telugu translation
docs.text:
1. Add a step named Translator (Claude with a glossary) between Set final status and Save to Notion. Add a Code node named Parse translation after it.
  2. Put prices, product names and disclaimers in the glossary so they stay exact.
  3. Test with a request that contains a price and a disclaimer. Confirm both appear unchanged in the Telugu output.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem What to check API call fails with an authentication error The key is correct and stored as a secret API call fails with a credit error Your Anthropic account has credit n8n cannot read the writer's reply The writer step must return valid JSON; check the parse step Nothing appears in Notion The Notion credential has access to the table

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text:
• About FreshFlow Software
  • Brand guide
  • Compliance rules
  • How the pipeline uses the rules
  • Examples
  • Limits

The writer step follows the brand guide. The checker step tests every draft against the 10 compliance rules. FreshFlow Software is a made-up company, so these rules are written for this demo.

docs.title: About FreshFlow Software
docs.text: FreshFlow makes software that helps food and manufacturing businesses in India manage stock, orders and production. Typical customers are sweet makers, packaged snack companies and distributors.

docs.title: Brand guide
docs.text: Area Guide Tone Friendly, clear and confident. Write like a helpful expert, not a salesperson Sentences Short and simple. One idea in each sentence Words to use simple, reliable, save time, track, plan, easy Words to avoid best in the world, revolutionary, guaranteed, 100%, magic, cheapest Ending Always end with one clear next step, such as "Book a demo."

docs.title: Compliance rules
docs.text: # Rule What it means in practice 1 Do not make claims you cannot prove Use numbers or percentages only if they come from an approved source 2 Never promise or guarantee results No "you will save X" or "guaranteed growth" 3 Any price must carry a disclaimer Add: "Prices may change. Contact sales for a current quote." 4 Do not name or compare competitors No brand names, no "better than" comparisons 5 Do not say the software makes a business "FSSAI compliant" Say it "helps track" records instead 6 Do not use customer names or quotes without approval Needs written approval first 7 Do not make health claims about any food product No "healthy", "good for digestion" or similar claims 8 Do not include personal details of real people No names, phone numbers or addresses 9 A human must review every AI-written piece before it is published The pipeline never publishes on its own 10 Every piece must end with a call to action For example, "Book a demo."

docs.title: How the pipeline uses the rules
docs.text:
1. The writer drafts the content using the brand guide and the rules.
  2. The checker tests the draft against all 10 rules.
  3. The result is one of three statuses:
  4. Approved: no rule is broken. A person still reviews it before publishing (rule 9).
  5. Refused: the request cannot be written safely, or it has no facts to work from.
  6. Needs Human Review: the request is vague or the checker is unsure, for example a claim with no source.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Request Result Why "Say FreshFlow is guaranteed to cut costs by 40% and is better than competitors" Approved after rewrite. The checker removed the guarantee, the 40% claim and the competitor comparison, and explained this in Checker Notes Rules 1, 2, 4 A request that includes real product facts and ends with "Book a demo" Approved, with no changes None "Write a 2-line intro for stock tracking" with no product facts Refused. The checker asks for facts Rule 1

These are real results from test runs. Rule 3 (price disclaimer) and rule 5 (FSSAI wording) are written into the prompt but not yet tested.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The checker is an AI model and can miss problems. Rule 9 is the safety net.
  • These rules are for a demo company and are not legal advice.

docs.title: Set up FreshFlow on Linux with Docker
docs.text: This guide shows you how to run FreshFlow on a Linux machine with Docker. You use GitHub Codespaces, so you need no install on your own computer. At the end, a test request creates a new row in your Notion table.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  • A GitHub account with Codespaces. The free plan gives 120 core hours a month, which is about 60 hours on the default 2-core codespace.
  • A web browser.
  • An Anthropic API key.
  • A Notion integration token, and the FreshFlow Content Review table shared with that integration.
  • The workflow file docs/freshflow-workflow.json in your repo.

Keep your keys private

Paste your API key and your Notion token only into the credential boxes in n8n. Never put them in a file, in your repo, in the terminal or in a screenshot. Treat your webhook path like a password too: paste it only into the terminal with read -rs, and never into a file or a screenshot.

docs.title: 1. Open a Linux terminal
docs.text:
1. Open your FreshFlow repo on GitHub.
  2. Click Code, then the Codespaces tab.
  3. Click Create codespace on main.

A code editor opens in your browser. At the bottom you should see a terminal with a prompt that ends in (main) $.

docs.title: 2. Check that Docker is installed
docs.text:
In the terminal, run:

docker --version

You should see a line that starts with Docker version.

Then run:

docker ps

You should see only a header line (CONTAINER ID, IMAGE, and so on). An empty list means no container is running. If you see an error instead, close the terminal, open a new one and run the command again.

docs.title: 3. Create a storage volume
docs.text:
n8n keeps your workflows and credentials in a Docker volume. Run:

docker volume create n8n_data

You should see n8n_data printed on the next line.

docs.title: 4. Download n8n
docs.text:
Run:

docker pull docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n

This takes 1 to 3 minutes. You should see many lines that end with Pull complete, and a last line that starts with Status:. If the image is already on the machine, the last line says Status: Image is up to date. This is also correct.

docs.title: 5. Start n8n
docs.text:
Run this as one line:

docker run -it --rm --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -e GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata -e TZ=Asia/Kolkata -e N8N_ENFORCE_SETTINGS_FILE_PERMISSIONS=true -e N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED=true -e N8N_PROXY_HOPS=1 -e WEBHOOK_URL="https://${CODESPACE_NAME}-5678.${GITHUB_CODESPACES_PORT_FORWARDING_DOMAIN}/" -e N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL="https://${CODESPACE_NAME}-5678.${GITHUB_CODESPACES_PORT_FORWARDING_DOMAIN}/" -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n

If you are not in India, change the two timezone values (GENERIC_TIMEZONE and TZ) to your own, for example Europe/London.

Wait about 30 seconds. You should see a line that starts with Version: and the line Editor is now accessible via.

The terminal stays busy while n8n runs. Do not close it and do not press Ctrl + C.

Note

You may see notices about settings that will change in a future version. They are not errors. A pop-up may say that port 5678 is available. Close the pop-up and do not click Make Public.

docs.title: 6. Open n8n in your browser
docs.text:
1. In the panel at the bottom, click the Ports tab.
  2. Find port 5678. Check that Visibility says Private.
  3. Hover over the address and click the globe icon (Open in Browser).

You should see the page Set up owner account.

  1. Enter your email, your name and a new password. This account lives only inside your own n8n.
  2. Click Next. If n8n asks questions about you, click Get started. If it offers a free licence key, click Skip.

You should see the n8n home page with an empty list of workflows.

docs.title: 7. Import the workflow
docs.text:
1. In the left menu, click +, then Workflow.
  2. Click the three dots (...) next to the workflow name, then Import from URL.
  3. Enter this address:
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karicherlamahesh-hub/freshflow-ai-content-pipeline/main/docs/freshflow-workflow.json

If you use your own copy of the repo, replace karicherlamahesh-hub with your GitHub user name. The repo must be public, or the address will not open.

You should see the workflow with the nodes Webhook, Writer, Checker, Translation, Save to Notion and Save error to Notion. Some nodes have a red mark because they have no credentials yet.

docs.title: 8. Add your credentials
docs.text:
1. Double-click the Writer node.
  2. Next to Credential, click Connect to Anthropic, then create a new credential.
  3. Paste your API key into API Key and click Save.
  4. Open the Checker node and the Translation node. In each one, choose the same credential from the Credential list.
  5. Double-click Save to Notion. Open the Credential list, click Create new credential, paste your token into Internal Integration Secret and click Save.
  6. Double-click Save error to Notion and choose the same Notion credential from the Credential list.
  7. Press Ctrl + S.

You should see no red marks on the nodes.

docs.title: 9. Publish the workflow
docs.text:
Click Publish at the top right.

In a codespace you may see Connection lost at the top right instead of the Publish button. This is a known problem with the Codespaces proxy. Publish the workflow from the command line instead:

  1. In the terminal panel, click the + icon to open a second terminal.
  2. Run:
    ID=$(docker exec n8n n8n list:workflow | cut -d'|' -f1)
docker exec n8n n8n publish:workflow --id="$ID"

You should see a line that starts with Publishing workflow with ID:.

The list command prints one line for each workflow, in the form ID|name. The first command keeps only the part before the |. If you have more than one workflow, run docker exec n8n n8n list:workflow on its own, copy the ID of your FreshFlow workflow, and use it in place of "$ID".

docs.title: 10. Save your webhook path
docs.text:
Your workflow starts when a request reaches its webhook. You send the request from the terminal, so you need the path.

  1. In n8n, double-click the Webhook node.
  2. In the Path box, press Ctrl + A, then Ctrl + C. Close the node.

  3. In the second terminal, run:

    read -rs P

  4. Press Ctrl + Shift + V once to paste, then press Enter. Nothing shows on screen.

  5. Check the length:
    echo -n "$P" | wc -c

You should see 36. The path that n8n makes by itself has 36 characters. If you typed your own path, you will see a different number, and that is fine.

docs.title: Send a test request
docs.text:
In the second terminal, the one where you ran read -rs P, run this as one line. The variable P exists only in that terminal.

curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST "http://localhost:5678/webhook/$P" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"request":"Write a short LinkedIn post about FreshFlow batch tracking"}'

You should see:

{"message":"Workflow was started"}
HTTP 200

This means the workflow started. It is not finished yet. Wait 1 to 2 minutes.

docs.title: Check the result in Notion
docs.text:
Open your FreshFlow Content Review table. A new row should appear with your request.

Status What it means Approved The draft passed all rules. Refused The request gave no product facts, so FreshFlow wrote nothing. Needs human review The checker found a claim that the request does not support.

The request above has no product facts, so the status should be Refused. This is the correct result. It shows that FreshFlow refuses to invent facts.

If no new row appears after 2 minutes, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
When you finish:

  1. In the second terminal, run unset P to remove the webhook path from memory.
  2. In the first terminal, press Ctrl + C to stop n8n. Your workflow stays in the n8n_data volume.
  3. Stop your codespace. Open github.com/codespaces, click the three dots next to your codespace, and click Stop codespace. This saves your free hours.

To use it again later, open the codespace from the same page and start n8n again with the command from step 5. Then repeat step 10, because the variable P is gone after you stop.

To learn more, see the API quick start and the API reference.

If a step fails, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Troubleshoot FreshFlow on Linux
docs.text:
This page lists the problems you are most likely to meet when you follow the setup guide. For each problem you see the symptom (what you notice), the cause (why it happens) and the fix.

Note

Never paste your API key, your Notion token or your webhook path into a file, a screenshot or a chat message while you fix a problem.

docs.title: n8n and the browser
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix n8n shows old workflows, not the new empty one You opened an older n8n tab, for example an n8n Cloud account, not the n8n in your codespace. Close that tab. In the Ports tab, find port 5678 and click the globe icon (Open in Browser). A new n8n shows Set up owner account. Connection lost appears at the top right of the n8n editor, and the terminal repeats Origin header does NOT match the expected origin The Codespaces proxy changes the address that the browser reports (the origin), so n8n refuses the live connection. The settings WEBHOOK_URL and N8N_PROXY_HOPS from the setup guide do not fix this. Keep working. The editor still saves your changes and n8n still runs. Do the steps that need the live connection, such as publishing, from the terminal. See the next row. The Publish button is missing The editor hides it while the connection is lost. Open a second terminal and run docker exec n8n n8n list:workflow. Each line shows the workflow ID, then a vertical bar, then the name. Copy the ID of your FreshFlow workflow, which is the part before the vertical bar. Then run docker exec n8n n8n publish:workflow --id="<ID>", and replace <ID> with that part.

docs.title: Terminal commands
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix 1s: command not found You typed the number 1 instead of the letter l. Type ls with a lowercase letter L. You typed a command and nothing appeared, not even a new prompt The command is waiting because you did not press Enter. Press Enter. Some commands wait on purpose: read -rs P shows nothing while it waits for you to paste, and the n8n terminal stays busy while n8n runs. The terminal says bash: read: ...: not a valid identifier You pasted the value on the same line as the read command. Run read -rs P alone and press Enter. The cursor waits. Then paste once with Ctrl + Shift + V and press Enter. The length check prints a number other than 36 The clipboard held other text, not the Path field of the Webhook node. Copy the Path field again. Run read -rs P again, paste once with Ctrl + Shift + V, and check the length again.

docs.title: The test request
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix The curl test returns HTTP 404 The workflow is not published, the path is wrong, or you used the webhook-test address, which works only while the editor listens. Publish the workflow (see the Publish row above). Check that the address uses /webhook/ and that $P has 36 characters. Then send the request again.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text:
1. Stop n8n with Ctrl + C in the first terminal.
  2. Start it again with the docker run command from step 5 of the setup guide. Your workflow stays in the n8n_data volume.
  3. Open n8n from the Ports tab and repeat the step where you were stuck.
